findings.where: First screen, Mark's photograph against the slate ground (worst at phone width, where his head floats above the heading; also desktop, around his hair and shoulder line; the 'Graded for the site' texture specimen shows a stepped slate edge cutting the lectern sign)
findings.fault: The purple backdrop has been keyed out to flat slate, not graded. Mark ends up as a hard-edged cut-out pasted onto a flat navy field. There is no light or depth around him, and nothing is left of the room he is speaking in, so it reads as a clipped head-and-shoulders, not a photograph of Mark at work.
findings.who_objects: The founder. The v7 card asks for the photograph to be graded into the house blue-grey as a full-bleed hero of Mark speaking, with real people in real light. A cut-out on a flat field looks cheap and slick, which the brief names as a failure. A development-bank visitor would also see a pasted-on figure, not a seasoned advisor in the room.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Write to me directly' contact block
findings.fault: The contact is a solid rectangle of full-strength house blue set on the muted slate. It is the most saturated and brightest area on the screen. It pulls the eye ahead of Mark's line and his face, and reads like an advertising banner, not one quiet contact.
findings.who_objects: The founder. The v7 card asks for 'one quiet contact', and the brief rules out anything salesy. A senior agency visitor would read the loud blue slab as a marketing call to action, which cuts against the personal-advisor tone.

findings.where: First screen, the logo in the header (mark and 'MMM INFRA' reversed to warm white)
findings.fault: The logo is shown in a reversed all-white version that Mark does not hold. The brand sheet records only the full-colour logo (blue wordmark, grey arches).
findings.who_objects: Mark. A version of his logo the client does not hold is made only with his yes, and none is recorded. Until he gives it, the first screen shows his mark in colours he has not approved.

findings.where: Article specimen, the numbers of the three-item list (also the 'PDF' row below, whose title is grey even though the whole row is the link)
findings.fault: Blue's declared job is 'only where something can be clicked', but the static list numbers are blue. The downloadable item is the opposite case: its whole row is a link, yet only the small 'PDF' label is blue. So blue does not reliably mean clickable on the article page.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles, who may tap a blue list number expecting a link, or miss that the lecture title itself opens the PDF. Angélique also loses a clear rule for when to use blue as she adds content.
